feat(cocod): let core enforce X-Cashu spending conditions

The previous cocod-v2 branch rejected creqB requests and any NUT-10 spending
condition at the daemon boundary. Both guards were correct for the stack they
targeted and are obsolete against this workspace:

- cashu-ts 4.5's creqB decoder hard-coded nut10: undefined, so a locked
  request round-tripped to an unlocked one. The workspace pins cashu-ts 5,
  whose TLV codec round-trips the nut10 option; a committed creqB fixture
  with a P2PK lock is parsed by real core (in-memory database) in the new
  test and classified as an enforceable P2PK condition.
- Core (since #309) resolves spendingCondition at parse, prepares locked
  outputs for P2PK, filters payableMints by NUT-11 support, and throws at
  prepare for unsupported or malformed conditions.

Keeping the daemon-side guards would duplicate core invariants and refuse
requests core pays correctly. What remains cocod's job is deciding how
core's rejection surfaces at the daemon API: map the unsupported/malformed
classification to a 400 with a clear reason before prepare (the daemon's
contract for invalid input) instead of a late 500. A route test pins that
prepare is never reached.

Refs #399

feat(cocod): migrate cocod to the Coco v2 API

Behavior-preserving port of every existing route and CLI command onto the
workspace core. Every hunk is forced by the v2 API shape, with one flagged
exception (shutdown disposal, below):

- Wallet init: SqliteRepositories({database}) is unchanged, but plugins now
  register through initializeCoco({plugins}) (a post-init use() would miss
  boot-time transport re-activation during recovery), and the npc plugin's v3
  API scopes accounts: NPCPlugin({defaultBaseUrl}) + addAccount({id, signer,
  useWebsocket}). initializeWallet returns {manager, npcAccount}; the account
  handle rides on UnlockedState so its presence is a type-level invariant.
- Mint/melt flows move to the canonical quote-before-prepare split:
  quotes.mint.create -> ops.mint.prepare({quote, amount}) and the melt twin
  (v2 PrepareMintInput/PrepareMeltInput take a quote reference).
- Balances: wallet.getBalances() is not reachable from the v2 facade; use
  wallet.balances.byMint() and report snapshot.total, which sums the same
  ready-proof set the v1 output contract was pinned against.
- Amount values JSON-serialize as strings in v2; call .toNumber() at every
  HTTP boundary to preserve the numeric wire format.
- npc routes call the account-scoped API instead of the removed
  manager.ext.npc accessors.
- /x-cashu/handle replaces the v1 cast with the v2 result union's
  discriminant check and drops an always-truthy dead check.
- Shutdown disposes the manager raced against a 3s timeout. This is the one
  deliberate divergence beyond the API port: this migration is what makes
  the manager own background watchers, processors, and per-account plugin
  websockets from boot, so releasing them on stop pairs with the new
  acquisition. The timer is cleared and a timeout win is logged.

New tests pin the migration itself: balance snapshot totals, the canonical
quote splits for receive/send bolt11, numeric receive output, and the inband
settlement path. Known behavior delta vs cocod master, unavoidable under the
v2 balance API: an empty wallet returns {} from /balance (v1 listed known
mints at 0).

feat(cocod): wire cocod into the bun workspace

- Mark the package private: it is not published from this repo; releases and
  changesets ignore it (check-release skips private packages).
- Replace the retired v1 coco-cashu-* npm dependencies with workspace:* deps
  on @cashu/coco-core and @cashu/coco-sqlite-bun, and move the npc plugin to
  its v3 release line. workspace:* (rather than the repo's exact-literal
  convention) because that convention exists to satisfy check-release for
  published packages; cocod is exempt, and workspace:* can never silently
  resolve to an npm version across release bumps. Happy to switch styles if
  preferred.
- Rename the lint script to typecheck so scripts/build.ts discovers it; drop
  the package-level format script and prettier/@types/bun devDependencies in
  favour of the repo root's tooling (the root pins @types/bun, which tsc
  auto-includes).
- Reformat the package with the repo prettier config (single quotes).

The npc plugin dependency stays on npm (it lives outside this repo). Its
current release declares an exact peer on a core release candidate, so bun
prints an unmet-peer warning against workspace core; install still succeeds.
Follow-up tracked in #399 to re-cut the plugin with a range peer.

The source still imports the v1 package names, so this commit does not
typecheck on its own; the next commit migrates the code to the v2 API.

feat(cocod): import cocod daemon and CLI from Egge21M/cocod

Snapshot of https://github.com/Egge21M/cocod at master (c9da575), imported

This commit intentionally does not build: dependencies still point at the

into the workspace and migrate it to the Coco v2 API, keeping the import
diff reviewable separately from every deliberate change.

fix(core): serialize receive prepare per mint to prevent NUT-13 counter collisions

The per-mint MintScopedLock was added for proof selection, so the send and melt
services (which select wallet-owned inputs) acquire it; receive, which swaps the
proofs carried in the received token, was left out. But the lock is held across
prepare(), which also performs the shared, non-atomic NUT-13 counter
read/derive/increment in createOutputsAndIncrementCounters, and receive consumes
that same per-keyset counter.

With no lock, two receive operations on the same mint (for example the same
gift-wrapped token delivered more than once, or two tokens arriving together)
read the same counter value, derive identical blinded outputs, and the second
write collides on the unique proof key, surfacing as "Failed to persist proofs
for 1 keyset group(s)".

Acquire the shared MintScopedLock in prepare() around the counter-consuming
section, mirroring the send/melt/mint services, and wire the shared instance
through Manager. Adds a regression test that fails without the lock.

fix(core): rollback releases original input proofs for swap-then-melt operations (#123)

* fix(core): release original input proofs on swap-then-melt rollback

When a swap-then-melt operation is rolled back before execute(),
getMeltInputSecrets() returns swap send secrets that don't exist yet
(swap hasn't been executed). restoreProofsToReady() silently skips
non-existent proofs, leaving original input proofs permanently
reserved with usedByOperationId.

Fix: in rollback(), when needsSwap is true, also call releaseProofs()
on inputProofSecrets to clear usedByOperationId. This is safe for
both pre-execute (proofs are ready+reserved → released) and
post-execute (proofs are spent → clearing reservation is harmless
since spent proofs are never returned by getReadyProofs()).
